content: The test image shows: a stem near the soil line with **white cottony mycelium** and **dark round/irregular sclerotia** embedded in it. This pattern strongly suggests either Southern Blight or Sclerotinia Timber Rot. Let me check reference images for both, plus a few other candidates.

- Test image: stem near soil line with **white cottony mycelium** and **dark gray/black round sclerotia** embedded in it
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/Bugwood_16 shows identical dark irregular Sclerotinia sclerotia (Bugwood series 5593XXX, same as test image 5593846)
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/Bugwood_23 shows exact same pattern: stems covered in white mycelium with developing dark sclerotia
- Southern Blight references show tan/brown sclerotia and wide field shots — no match to test image's dark sclerotia
- Alternaria shows dark stem canker, no white mycelium — ruled out
- Gray Mold shows fruit lesion — ruled out

The test image most closely matches Sclerotinia Timber Rot: white cottony mycelium on stem with dark black/gray sclerotia.
